question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $2$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{5}+2 & =\frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{x}{5}+2-2 & =\frac{2}{3}-2 \\ \frac{x}{5}+0 & =\frac{2}{3}-\frac{6}{3} \\ \frac{x}{5} & =-\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, multiplying both sides of the equation by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{5} & =-\frac{4}{3} \\ \cancel{5}\cdot \frac{x}{\cancel{5}} & =5\cdot (-\frac{4}{3}) \\ x & =-\frac{20}{3}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
